True scale: three model figures on an empty table

Vertical 9:16 photograph. A huge matte black tabletop stretches away into darkness. In the centre, very small, stand three 1:87 model-railway figures: an adult, a second adult, and a child holding a hand, with a tiny suitcase beside them. A single cold fluorescent teal light from above makes a small pool around them; everything beyond falls to black, so the empty table looks endless and ready to be filled. Shot low on a 50mm macro lens, shallow focus, the figures sharp and the table's dust and scratches visible. Cheap colour negative film at night, visible grain, slight halation round the light. Painted plastic figures, no faces readable. No text. Thanks.
One room from the ceiling: a B&B at night

Vertical 9:16 photograph looking straight down from the ceiling of one small bed-and-breakfast room in an English town at night. A double bed and a travel cot fill nearly the whole floor; between them a narrow strip of worn carpet with bin bags of clothes, a pushchair folded against the wall, a kettle and cereal boxes on the floor because there is no kitchen. Two adults and a small child asleep under the duvet, turned away, only hair and shapes. The only light is a buzzing fluorescent tube by the door, cold teal, with the rest in shadow. 28mm lens, slight wide-angle bend at the edges. Night colour film, heavy grain, muddy blacks. Thanks.
A household as its belongings in an empty car park

Vertical 9:16 photograph at night in an empty multi-storey car park in England. In one painted parking bay, everything one family owns is lined up neatly on the concrete: six black bin bags, a child's scooter, a folded cot, a microwave, two duvets in a laundry bag, a school uniform on a hanger hooked over a pushchair. No people. One cold fluorescent teal tube overhead lights only this bay; the rows of empty bays behind fade into dark. Oil stains, a puddle reflecting the light, a faded bay line. Shot from a standing height on a 35mm lens. Cheap colour film, grain, slight halation, lonely and quiet. No readable text. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 night photograph from a drone high above an empty English retail-park car park. Every parking bay and the road beyond is filled with small packed suitcases and holdalls, stood upright in tight rows, one per family, thousands upon thousands running past the edge of the frame into the dark. At the bottom edge, a single red-brick terraced house with one lit window gives the scale. Cold fluorescent teal from tall car-park lamps, pools of light falling off into black, wet tarmac. Shot on cheap 35mm colour negative film, heavy grain, slight blur, muted greens, no people visible, no signage or logos. Lonely, quiet, slightly eerie. Thanks.
The B&B key board that never ends

Vertical 9:16 photograph inside the reception of a cheap English bed-and-breakfast at night. Behind an empty wooden counter with a brass bell, a wall of numbered room keys on hooks, each with a worn plastic fob, runs up past the ceiling and back down a narrow corridor into darkness, rows multiplying until they blur into a texture. One key fob in the foreground, sharp, is stamped in plain black numerals "134,210". A single flickering fluorescent tube gives cold teal light, magnolia walls, swirly carpet, fire-door sign without words. 35mm lens, cheap colour film, grain, faint halation, no people. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 photograph, close and slightly overhead, of a large paper map of England pinned to a cork board on a council office wall after hours. The map is crowded with small teal map pins, so dense around London, Birmingham, Manchester and the coast towns that the pins merge into solid glittering crusts and the printed roads disappear beneath them; thinner scatterings reach every county. A desk lamp is off; the only light is a buzzing fluorescent tube overhead, cold teal, with the pins casting tiny shadows. Shallow depth of field, 50mm, cheap colour film, grain, slight vignette. No text, no people, no logos. Thanks.
The dark city of empties (aerial true scale)

Vertical 9:16 aerial photograph at night, looking straight down from very high over an endless grid of English Victorian brick terraced streets, rows of slate roofs and back yards running to the edge of the frame in every direction, every house dark, windows sealed with grey perforated steel security screens, no lights on anywhere. In the lower left corner, one small patch of the grid glows cold fluorescent teal: a few streets of tiny lit windows, small enough to cover with a thumb, utterly outnumbered by the darkness around it. Shot on cheap 35mm colour negative film pushed two stops, heavy grain, slight halation round the teal, faint motion blur, no people visible. Thanks.
The key wall (every empty house as a key)

Vertical 9:16 photograph at night inside a shabby English lettings office after closing, a single flickering fluorescent tube overhead throwing cold teal light. The whole back wall, floor to ceiling and receding down a long corridor into darkness, is pegboard hung with thousands upon thousands of identical brass Yale-style house keys on small paper tags, each one for a house nobody lives in, dust on the tags, keys untouched for months. At the bottom of the frame, on a worn grey carpet tile, one small cardboard box of a few keys, lit brighter, looking tiny against the wall. No people. Cheap colour negative film, grain, slight green-teal cast, lonely and eerie. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 photograph at night in an empty English community hall, folding chairs stacked against the wall, one fluorescent strip light overhead casting cold teal. On a long trestle table stretching away from camera sits a vast architectural model: rows and rows of tiny unpainted grey card terraced houses packed shoulder to shoulder to the far end of the table and spilling onto a second table, every one dark. In the near corner a much smaller cluster of tiny model figures, lit teal, dwarfed. A hand-lettered card propped at the front reads "303,185". Shot on cheap colour negative film with a 35mm lens, low angle, shallow depth of field, heavy grain, scuffed lino floor. Thanks.
True-scale diorama: the fourth block lights up

Vertical 9:16 night photograph of a huge model-railway diorama on a warehouse floor, seen from a low, level camera. Rows of tiny grey English terraced houses, thousands of them, laid out in four rectangular blocks. Front left, one small cluster of houses lit cold fluorescent teal from a single overhead tube: the homeless households. Behind it, two long blocks of dark, unlit houses. Beyond those, a fourth block the same size again where every tiny window glows warm amber with a lamp left on, curtains half drawn, no figures anywhere. The teal cluster looks small now, roughly a quarter of everything else. Shot on CineStill 800T, 35mm lens, visible grain, halation round the windows, slightly underexposed, dust on the model roofs. Thanks.
A seaside town lit for nobody

Vertical 9:16 night photograph from a hillside above a small English harbour town out of season, January. Steep rows of painted fishermen's cottages and newer holiday flats tumble down to a dark harbour, and nearly every window is lit warm and identical by a timer lamp, yet the streets are completely empty, no cars moving, no one on the quay. In the foreground, at the bottom of the frame, one cold teal fluorescent doorway of a run-down guesthouse used as a hostel, a single tiny silhouette standing in it. The brightest town you have ever seen, and nobody home. Shot on Kodak Portra 800 pushed two stops, 50mm, handheld, heavy grain, mist off the sea, slight motion softness. Thanks.
A wall of key safes, counted

Vertical 9:16 night photograph of a long, wet London-brick wall lit by one buzzing teal fluorescent tube, covered top to bottom in a tight grid of hundreds of small black combination key safes, the kind screwed beside the front doors of short lets, their dials catching the light, every one shut, the grid running out of frame on all sides as if it never ends. Stencilled once in white paint across the bricks near the bottom, slightly flaked: "267,894". No people, a puddle on the pavement reflecting the teal. Documentary street photography, shot on CineStill 800T, 28mm lens, slight vignette, coarse grain, a little camera tilt, cheap and cold. Thanks.
